focus: A WHY is discovered in patterns from lived experience rather than invented as a branding sentence. A reader learns to search for recurring moments of contribution and impact before writing purpose language.
coreClaim: The Origins of a WHY turns origin story into a practical decision rule backed by named cases and checkable details.

centralConcept.name: origin story
centralConcept.plainDefinition: A WHY is discovered in patterns from lived experience rather than invented as a branding sentence.
centralConcept.whyItMatters: A reader learns to search for recurring moments of contribution and impact before writing purpose language.

keyClaims: origin story becomes usable only when tied to visible behavior.
Simon Sinek career background gives the first concrete anchor.
Wright brothers workshop roots creates contrast so the idea is not one anecdote.
Howard Schultz and Starbucks experience adds a boundary case for application.
Past patterns, Contribution, Impact, WHY statement keep the unit from collapsing into generic purpose talk.

namedExamples.label: Simon Sinek career background
namedExamples.summary: Simon Sinek's background includes Brandeis University, advertising work, and Columbia University teaching. The personal-origin case keeps discovery tied to lived patterns.
namedExamples.teachesWhat: Simon Sinek career background turns Simon Sinek into a concrete test of the unit's central mechanism.

namedExamples.label: Wright brothers workshop roots
namedExamples.summary: Wilbur Wright and Orville Wright brought bicycle-shop mechanics to the Kitty Hawk flight problem. The case shows origin patterns becoming a cause.
namedExamples.teachesWhat: Wright brothers workshop roots turns Wright brothers into a concrete test of the unit's central mechanism.

namedExamples.label: Howard Schultz and Starbucks experience
namedExamples.summary: Howard Schultz linked Seattle Starbucks to an experience-centered 1980s retail idea shaped by the espresso bar model. The case shows personal experience shaping organizational meaning.
namedExamples.teachesWhat: Howard Schultz and Starbucks experience turns Howard Schultz into a concrete test of the unit's central mechanism.

hardEdge: The tempting misread is to turn origin story into a universal slogan and ignore the cases. The stricter reading keeps the claim tied to the specific examples and uses the framework only where the details support it.
voiceCues: plain business language with short contrasts
forbiddenLeakage: Do not turn the close into external rivalry
paraphraseNotes: The Origins of a WHY works from origin story: A WHY is discovered in patterns from lived experience rather than invented as a branding sentence. A reader learns to search for recurring moments of contribution and impact before writing purpose language. Simon Sinek's background includes Brandeis University, advertising work, and Columbia University teaching. The personal-origin case keeps discovery tied to lived patterns. Wilbur Wright and Orville Wright brought bicycle-shop mechanics to the Kitty Hawk flight problem. The case shows origin patterns becoming a cause. Howard Schultz linked Seattle Starbucks to an experience-centered 1980s retail idea shaped by the espresso bar model. The case shows personal experience shaping organizational meaning. Past patterns starts the local logic for The Origins of a WHY; Contribution, Impact, WHY statement complete the sequence. Keep Sinek, Wright, and Schultz on origins from lived patterns; external rivalry is not the closing measure yet.

testableFacts.claim: Simon Sinek career background makes origin story concrete through Simon Sinek and Brandeis University.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because Simon Sinek gives the idea a visible setting, the reader can test the claim against behavior instead of accepting a slogan.
testableFacts.commonError: The safe move is to treat Simon Sinek career background as colorful background.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: The case carries the mechanism, so treating it as decoration removes the lesson's evidence.

testableFacts.claim: Wright brothers workshop roots adds a second anchor for origin story with Wilbur Wright and Orville Wright.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Since a second case repeats the pattern in a different venue, the mechanism is less likely to be a one-off anecdote.
testableFacts.commonError: One example is enough to prove the whole model.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: One example can illustrate; comparison is what exposes the transferable pattern.

testableFacts.claim: Howard Schultz and Starbucks experience supplies a third checkable scene using Howard Schultz and Seattle Starbucks.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because the third scene changes the cast and setting, the writer can vary examples without inventing a new case.
testableFacts.commonError: A third case should simply repeat the first case's lesson.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: The third case should test a neighboring misconception, not restamp the same sentence.

testableFacts.claim: origin story depends on the sequence Past patterns before Contribution.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because the first term frames the second, reversing them makes the visible tactic carry a job it cannot carry alone.
testableFacts.commonError: Order is stylistic, so any sequence works if the message sounds polished.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: Order changes diagnosis; a polished tactic cannot repair a wrong premise.

testableFacts.claim: Past patterns, Contribution, Impact, WHY statement form the local framework for The Origins of a WHY.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because each member names a different job, the writer can assign claims to distinct functions rather than blending them.
testableFacts.commonError: The framework is a slogan and can be shortened to one word.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: Shortening removes the distinctions the quiz and examples need to test.

testableFacts.claim: advertising is a hard detail that should stay attached to Simon Sinek career background.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because hard specifics are portable only inside their case, moving advertising to another example creates false grounding.
testableFacts.commonError: Any true detail can be reused wherever it sounds useful.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: A true detail becomes misleading when it is attached to the wrong case.

testableFacts.claim: bicycle shop gives Wright brothers workshop roots a different factual token from Simon Sinek career background.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Since the factual token is different, comparison can teach contrast rather than repeating a generic success story.
testableFacts.commonError: All business examples can use the same date-place-scale language.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: Generic stamping makes real cases feel invented and blurs the chapter-specific spine.

testableFacts.claim: 1980s retail idea helps mark the boundary of origin story.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because boundary details tell the reader where the idea stops, they prevent overgeneralizing from a single attractive case.
testableFacts.commonError: A useful concept should apply the same way to every named organization.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: The mechanism changes by venue; boundary details keep the application honest.

testableFacts.claim: The Origins of a WHY should teach origin story through Simon Sinek career background, Wright brothers workshop roots, and Howard Schultz and Starbucks experience, not through generic leadership advice.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because three named anchors carry separate hard specifics, the unit can make a testable claim without inventing scenes.
testableFacts.commonError: Purpose language alone is enough to ground a leadership lesson.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: Purpose language without checkable anchors becomes motivational abstraction.
